brief: Goldman's Eric Sheridan raised the humanoid robot forecast in an 80-page Physical AI note. The base case moves to 75,000 shipments in 2026, 890,000 units in 2030 and 6.5 million in 2035, against a prior 51,000, 256,000 and 1.4 million, a $138 billion market by 2035. Five conclusions carry the upgrade. Logistics and warehouses adopt first because eCommerce and retail already automate, so Goldman frames about 5.6% of Amazon's total cost to serve as automatable by 2030, worth roughly $72 billion of savings and a 240 basis point EBIT margin tailwind in its upside case. Autos follow, where welding is automated but final assembly and parts sorting are manual, so humanoids priced at $20,000 to $60,000 adopted at 10% to 50% rates would add 1% to 6% of gross operating margin, less if savings pass to buyers. Humanoid mobility shifts control from hardware PLCs to virtual PLCs growing 20% to 30% a year, which questions the lock-in of Siemens, Rockwell and Schneider. Each robot carries $3,000 to $6,000+ of semiconductor content. A Goldman survey found ~40% of respondents expect at least 10% of workflows automated in 3-5 years.
